checks.scope: Iterated collections and key-addressed maps have distinct named shapes.
checks.observable: Observe the value's iteration or key-lookup use, then compare the id's noun shape.
checks.consistency: Fits DP-19's value naming and AP-66's avoidance of representation suffixes.
checks.exceptions: Plural collection nouns and discriminator heads are explicitly retained.
checks.fix: Use plural item names for collections and a meaningful mapping name for keyed maps.
checks.expression: The collection-versus-map distinction makes the convention more precise than a blanket plural rule.

rationale: tasks describes a collection; domain_to_range describes a keyed map. An array implementation alone need not appear in the identifier.

checks.scope: I/O identifiers encode semantic values rather than direction or representation.
checks.observable: Check declared ids, true input/output pass-through, and the enumerated generic-name cases.
checks.consistency: AP-43's path-id subcase overlaps here, but the rule's own naming checks remain coherent.
checks.exceptions: External spellings, plural collections, and qualified head-noun phrases are expressly retained.
checks.fix: Rename and unify a shared concept at its owning contract rather than copy caller-specific names.
checks.expression: The explicit examples make this a house naming convention, not a claim that every one-word noun is inherently ambiguous.

rationale: The criterion is decidable as a stated convention; consolidation with AP-43 is reported under the duplicate owner rather than recasting the convention as a logical error.

checks.scope: Rule slugs are evaluated for an available equally clear affirmative invariant.
checks.observable: Compare candidate names against the rule's actual trigger and obligation.
checks.consistency: DP-19 explicitly makes positive rule names a clarity preference, not an absolute prohibition.
checks.exceptions: Intentional clear negations are retained rather than mechanically renamed.
checks.fix: Rename only when the affirmative form preserves or improves clarity.
checks.expression: A qualitative comparison is appropriate here; a numeric name-length threshold would not settle it.

rationale: This is a preference with an explicit clarity exception. never-resume may be clearer than an invented positive euphemism and need not be changed.

checks.scope: Technique claims about activity flow and human gates are the intended boundary.
checks.observable: Ask whether truth depends on the surrounding graph or on one local application.
checks.consistency: The 'no separate commit step follows' safe example asserts exactly the surrounding sequence being prohibited.
checks.exceptions: Local input iteration should also be explicit so AP-10's valid case survives.
checks.fix: Move actual routing/approval to activity structure and keep emitted evidence local.
checks.expression: Remove the graph-position example and qualify loop/iteration as activity-level.

rationale: Purpose words can be stage-neutral; a claim about which step follows the technique cannot be.
